title: A session is a record its store issued, and its backend is never the local tier
scope:
the mechanics [0012](0012.md) § 4 deferred — the member roster
`Core\Session` carries, the four operations a backend answers, which backends `[session] backend`
admits and how the excluded one is refused, when a record is read and written, and when it expires.
Not the *shape* of the class, which 0012 § 4 already fixed (a class, an explicit start, no ambient
array); not the seal on the cookie that carries the id, which is
[0060](0060.md) § 1's ring; not the strict-id rule, which is
[0124](0124.md) § 6; and not the ban on the local
tier itself, which is [0059](0059.md) § 4's and is only *enforced*
here.
dependsOnText:
[0059](0059.md), which decides what may not hold a
session and therefore what is left to choose between.

summary.headline: A session is a record its store issued, never kept on the local machine
summary.body:
A session is one record in a store that can answer whether it issued a given id, and an id the
store never issued is rejected. The store is the shared cache tier or the database. The local
tier is not allowed, and configuring it refuses at boot, because a session on one machine's disk
stops being a session once a second machine serves the site. The record is loaded once when the
session starts, written back whole when it changes, and expired by the store itself. No lock is
held across a request.
